items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Actually there’s a book that even mentions me that’s by Steven Isor called Songs of the Unsung: the Musical Journey of Horace Tapscott.

ctx.x: You know I mean he was like a cultural warrior and a well loved person and he passed away in February 1999. But he said you know art should be contributive. Not competitive. And he stayed in Los Angeles in the hood and nurtured a lot of people. And he didn’t leave the area to go to New York to become successful. And so, and he was around the time with like the Watts riots and you’d bring music on a flatbed truck, I mean sort of a jazz mobile. I’m not quite sure of the history. I mean I’m also kind of tired so…
What’s the effect of 80 cable channels, and constant music everywhere you go, on people’s attention span?
